title: Intro to VS Code
line: Open a folder, edit fast, then run and debug a small script.

project.title: A temperature converter, set up alone
project.brief: Start an empty folder on your own. Write temp.js that turns Celsius into Fahrenheit, add a README and workspace settings that format on save, and run it in the terminal.
checks: The folder holds temp.js, README.md and .vscode/settings.json
The workspace settings turn on editor.formatOnSave
node temp.js prints 212 for 100 degrees Celsius

lessons.title: Open a folder and make files
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner VS Code. Open a new folder named recipe-box, tour the Activity Bar and the Explorer, then make README.md and recipe.txt with six ingredient names, one per line.
lessons.passes: The recipe-box folder holds README.md and a recipe.txt with six lines.

lessons.title: The Command Palette and Quick Open
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code Command Palette (Shift+Cmd+P) and Quick Open (Cmd+P) by jumping between the two files and running Sort Lines Ascending on the ingredients in recipe.txt.
lessons.passes: The six lines of recipe.txt are in A to Z order.

lessons.title: Edit many lines at once
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code multi-cursor editing with Option+click, Cmd+D and Option+Cmd+Down by turning the six plain lines into recipe.json, an array of objects that each have a name and cups.
lessons.passes: recipe.json is valid JSON with six objects that each have name and cups.

lessons.title: Find and replace across files
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code find and replace in one file (Cmd+F) and across the whole folder (Shift+Cmd+F) by changing every cups to grams in recipe.json and README.md in one pass.
lessons.passes: No file in recipe-box holds the word cups and recipe.json is still valid JSON.

lessons.title: Run code in the integrated terminal
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code integrated terminal (Ctrl+`). Write scale.js that reads recipe.json and prints each amount doubled, run it with node, then split a second terminal beside the first.
lessons.passes: node scale.js prints six lines, each with twice the grams in recipe.json.

lessons.title: Jump around and rename safely
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code code navigation. Move the doubling into a function in its own file, jump to it with Go to Definition (F12) and rename it to scaleRecipe everywhere with Rename Symbol (F2).
lessons.passes: A function named scaleRecipe is defined in one file and called from scale.js.

lessons.title: Install an extension
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code Extensions view (Shift+Cmd+X) by installing Prettier, choosing it as the default formatter and running Format Document on scale.js.
lessons.passes: The Prettier extension is installed and scale.js matches its formatting.

lessons.title: Settings and format on save
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code settings (Cmd+,) and how user and workspace settings differ by adding .vscode/settings.json to recipe-box with format on save turned on and a tab size of 2.
lessons.passes: .vscode/settings.json sets editor.formatOnSave to true and editor.tabSize to 2.

lessons.title: Find a bug with a breakpoint
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code debugger. Set a breakpoint in scale.js, start it from Run and Debug with Node.js, step over lines and watch the variables to find why a new 250 gram item doubles to 250250.
lessons.passes: node scale.js prints 500 for the 250 gram item, not 250250.
